title: Cut didChange inline parse out of completion current-revision apply path
notes:
2026-03-17 progress:
- representative live traces after turn_wait and interactive apply fixes show that turn_wait is no longer the dominant systemic bottleneck; queue is typically empty (queued_completion_ahead=0, did_change_ahead=0, active_completion_count=0).
- remaining user-visible latency splits into three paths: (1) intermittent prepare_stateful failures in ~3-6s with empty completion queue, (2) exact current-revision wait deadline around 124-129ms producing fail_closed before the next request succeeds in ~6-8ms, (3) successful cold path still spending ~440-560ms in query_bundle plus ~105ms in collect.
- landed instrumentation in commit a7a94245: completion timeline now exports prepare_details (wait_budget_ms, min/observed versions, wait/snapshot elapsed, apply age start/terminal, outcome), and observability raw JSON exports config/effective/source for runtime knobs including BSL_INTELLISENSE_V2_INTERACTIVE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS.
- local checks found no workspace/user settings override for BSL_INTELLISENSE_V2_INTERACTIVE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS; live-only prepare_stateful overrun is therefore still unexplained.
Next resume step:
1. Reload VS Code window so the updated extension panel and rebuilt lsp-server are active.
2. Capture a new live completion trace that includes prepare_details and a new observability Raw JSON dump that includes config.
3. If prepare_details.wait_budget_ms is 120 while prepare_stateful still runs ~3s before failing, investigate timeout/cancellation enforcement inside prepare_stateful/wait_for_file_version rather than config.
4. If the effective budget in metrics/config is unexpectedly high, trace the runtime/config source path before further scheduler changes.
close_reason: Moved didChange current-revision apply ahead of inline parse, added regression coverage for delayed parse races, and verified p33_ plus p38 real-module revision-churn gate.

Scope:
- identify why completion wait_for_file_version can take multiple seconds even when queue backlog is empty
- tighten runtime/apply orchestration or priority so completion reaches current revision promptly
- add regression coverage that isolates wait_for_file_version latency from query_bundle and exact wait
close_reason: Implemented interactive apply path for LSP text sync and request-path fallback to cut wait_for_file_version lag; added regression test for interactive apply preempting background backlog.

title: Reduce completion turn_wait by early supersession of stale queued requests
description:

The next step is to reduce turn_wait without changing semantic correctness: stale queued completion requests should be superseded earlier, and queue discipline should prefer the freshest interactive completion for a file once newer didChange/completion intent is known.

Scope:
- identify which queued or active completion requests can be declared stale before semantic work starts
- reduce turn_wait by queue policy changes only, without weakening current-revision or exact contracts
- add dispatcher-level and integration tests that prove lower backlog pressure without semantic shortcuts
close_reason: Closed

title: Reduce completion first-response latency on real large modules
description:

The warm path is already healthy (~8ms), so the epic focuses on first-response availability and responsiveness on real large modules without relaxing the current-revision/fail-closed contract.

Evidence snapshot:
- turn_wait can consume ~95% of total request time before semantic work starts
- fail_closed currently comes from exact wait deadline, not wrong version or missing task
- successful cold responses still spend ~645ms in query_bundle + ~106ms in collect
- representative real-module gate must be the acceptance source of truth

This epic is planning/execution scaffolding linked to the approved architecture direction in OpenSpec and should drive the implementation graph once execution is approved.

close_reason: Epic complete: queue starvation, prepare/wait readiness, split head/exact completion routing, observability, acceptance evidence, delayed didChange parse handling, and cold query_bundle follow-up are all closed with representative real-conf_big validation. Final acceptance is recorded in refactor-v2-completion-dual-artifact-path evidence, and remaining child tasks now all have concrete closure evidence including p37/p38 live reports and targeted p33 regressions.

title: p31: исследование задержки ожидания type_index в warm+churn
description:
Контекст:
- Прогон p31 (large_warm, churn_every=10) стабильно показывает общий warm elapsed ~415-418s при 55 completion.
- По gate report узкое место в large/warm: completion p95 ~34.4s, index_fetch p95 ~34.4s, index_fetch_wait p95 ~34.3s, parse_result p95 ~0ms, build_total p95 ~20-22ms.
- Start/cold фазы отдельно имеют parse/query доминирование ~35s, но ключевая деградация under churn в warm — именно ожидание перед исполнением type_index.
- block_on/cancellation сигналы не объясняют задержку (block_on_total=0, cancelled_rate=0), revision_delta p95=0.

Что уже сделано:
- Добавлены deep метрики type_index fetch (pre/inside/post salsa window, first/last event deltas, revision markers, per-fetch counters).
- Добавлен timeline capture через env BSL_V2_TYPE_INDEX_FETCH_TIMELINE_MAX_EVENTS.
- Снижен шум тестового вывода: slow WARN теперь по умолчанию выключен при наличии BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_GATE_REPORT, короткий p31 progress оставлен включенным.

Что делать дальше (продолжение root-cause):
1) Инструментировать didChange/apply pipeline таймингами с корреляцией по revision: queue_wait, apply_exec, snapshot/invalidations, publish-ready.
2) Добавить stage-метрики от revision after churn edit до first WillExecute(type_index) в следующем completion.
3) Разбить текущий index_fetch_wait на причины (apply backlog vs snapshot rebuild vs scheduling gap), чтобы убрать unattributed класс.
4) Прогнать матрицу подтверждения: no-churn, churn_every=1/5/10, и сравнить p95/p99 по новым stage-метрикам.
5) Зафиксировать критерий фикса: снижение large/warm index_fetch_wait p95 до целевого бюджета без регрессий small профиля.

Артефакты:
- Последний clean report: /tmp/p31-churn10-clean.json
- Команда clean прогона: BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_CHURN_MODE=large_warm BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_CHURN_EVERY=10 BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_PROGRESS_EVERY=10 BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_GATE_REPORT=/tmp/p31-churn10-clean.json cargo test -q -p bsl-backend --bin bsl-lsp-server p31_scale_aware_large_small_completion_gate_live -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
- Команда deep-clean (без WARN, с timeline): BSL_V2_TYPE_INDEX_FETCH_SLOW_LOG=0 BSL_V2_TYPE_INDEX_FETCH_TIMELINE_MAX_EVENTS=256 BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_CHURN_MODE=large_warm BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_CHURN_EVERY=10 BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_PROGRESS_EVERY=10 BSL_V2_SCALE_AWARE_GATE_REPORT=/tmp/p31-churn10-deep-clean.json cargo test -q -p bsl-backend --bin bsl-lsp-server p31_scale_aware_large_small_completion_gate_live -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
notes:
Локализация подтверждена по матрице /tmp/p31-matrix-{off,large-warm-e1,e5,e10}.json:
- no-churn: large/warm completion_p95 ~23ms, index_fetch_wait_p95=0ms.
- churn: large/warm completion_p95 и index_fetch_wait_p95 растут до ~35-59s при runtime_queue_wait_interactive_p95 <=2ms и runtime_apply_changes_queue_wait_p95 ~0ms.
- ключевые stage-метрики совпадают: first_check_to_first_execute_p95 == idle_before_first_execute_p95 == index_fetch_wait_p95 (e1/e5/e10).
Вывод: узкое место локализовано не в runtime очередях apply/dispatch и не в build_total, а в длительном idle-gap внутри owner_hint type-index fetch до первого WillExecute(type_index) под churn (pre-first-execute gap).
Рекомендованный следующий шаг: в perf scenarios (task 30j) и CI perf gate (task 3ks) использовать отдельный churn профиль и отдельный budget на этот stage-gap.
close_reason: Локализация root-cause подтверждена по p31 matrix: bottleneck в pre-first-execute idle-gap type_index fetch под churn; зафиксировано в notes с артефактами
